title: Germany Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Blue Card & Chancenkarte
metaDescription: Germany skilled worker visa 2026: EU Blue Card thresholds €50,700 and €45,934, the Chancenkarte points system, recognition rules and how to apply.
headline: Germany Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Routes Explained

sections.title: The EU Blue Card: the fast route for graduates
sections.content:
The EU Blue Card remains the primary route for highly qualified workers. It needs a recognised or comparable foreign university degree, a concrete job offer matching the qualification that lasts at least six months, and a salary above the annual threshold. In 2026 the general threshold is €50,700 gross per year, while the reduced threshold for shortage occupations, recent graduates and IT specialists without a degree is €45,934.20.

IT professionals without a degree can now qualify with at least three years of relevant experience within the last seven years plus Federal Employment Agency approval. Blue Card holders can apply for permanent settlement after 21 months with B1 German, or after 27 months with A1 German, provided they have paid pension contributions for that period.

sections.title: The skilled worker permit for recognised qualifications
sections.content:
Under the Skilled Immigration Act, you count as a skilled worker if you hold a German vocational qualification or degree, or a foreign one recognised as equivalent or comparable. There is no general salary threshold for this permit, with one exception: if you are 45 or older when your first permit is issued, you must earn at least €55,770 a year in 2026 or prove adequate retirement provision.

Check your qualification early through the official anerkennung-in-deutschland.de portal, starting with the Anabin database and the ZAB where needed. Permits for contracts shorter than four years are issued for the contract term plus six months, for at most four years, under a change in force since 29 July 2026.

sections.title: The Chancenkarte: job hunting without an offer
sections.content:
The Chancenkarte, or Opportunity Card, is a points-based residence permit that lets qualified professionals come to Germany for up to 12 months to look for work without a job offer first. Fully recognised skilled workers qualify without points. Everyone else needs a foreign degree or at least two years of vocational training recognised where it was earned, German at A1 or English at B2, and at least 6 points.

Points come from partial recognition of the qualification (4 points), German at B2 (3 points), B1 (2) or A2 (1), English at C1 (1 point), and professional experience of five years within the last seven (3 points) or two years within the last five (2 points). You must also prove funds of about €1,091 a month, or a blocked account holding €13,092 for a year, and you may work up to 20 hours a week while searching.

sections.title: How to apply and what it costs
sections.content:
Applications go through the German embassy or consulate in your country, increasingly via the Federal Foreign Office Consular Services Portal. The national visa fee is €75 and the residence title costs €100. The minimum wage in Germany is €13.90 gross per hour since 1 January 2026, rising to €14.60 from 1 January 2027.

Prepare a recognised qualification, a valid passport, proof of funds and health insurance, and a job contract or points evidence depending on the route. Processing times vary by embassy, so apply early, keep every document in the original plus a certified translation, and verify the current thresholds before you submit, because the pension ceiling they are tied to rises every year.

faqs.q: What is the EU Blue Card salary threshold in Germany in 2026?
faqs.a: The general EU Blue Card threshold in Germany in 2026 is €50,700 gross per year. A reduced threshold of €45,934.20 applies to shortage occupations, graduates within three years of their degree, and IT specialists without a degree who have at least three years of relevant experience. Always verify the current figure with the Federal Foreign Office before applying.

faqs.q: What is the Chancenkarte and who qualifies?
faqs.a: The Chancenkarte is a residence permit that lets you search for work in Germany for up to 12 months without a job offer. You need a foreign degree or two years of vocational training, German at A1 or English at B2, at least 6 points, and proof of €1,091 a month in funds. Fully recognised skilled workers qualify without points.

faqs.q: Do I need German to work in Germany?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. The Blue Card has no general language requirement, though German helps with settlement after 21 months. The Chancenkarte requires German at A1 or English at B2 as a minimum. Learning German to B1 speeds up permanent settlement and opens far more jobs, because many employers outside international tech teams work in German.

faqs.q: How long does a Germany work visa take?
faqs.a: Processing times vary widely by embassy and route, from a few weeks to several months. Blue Card applications are usually faster because the job offer and salary are already fixed, while Chancenkarte and recognition cases take longer. Apply early, submit complete documents, and use the Consular Services Portal where your embassy offers it.
